ceviri.20: What tools and what steps go into a technical SEO analysis?
ceviri.21: The audit starts by going through Search Console data and the server logs; crawler tools and speed tests are added to that. Indexing blockers come first, then performance, and structured data gaps last, in that order.
ceviri.22: What's the difference between technical SEO and content SEO, and which comes first?
ceviri.23: Content SEO is concerned with what a page says, technical SEO with how the page is reached. A page that can't be crawled won't be rewarded in the rankings however well it is written; that's why the technical foundations are made solid first.
ceviri.24: If site speed (Core Web Vitals) is poor, how does that affect rankings?
ceviri.25: Core Web Vitals is a ranking signal in its own right; weak performance drops a page behind its competitors. A weakened user experience pushes the bounce rate up, which sends the search engine a negative signal in turn.
ceviri.26: Why do the sitemap and robots.txt files matter, and what happens if they're set up wrongly?
ceviri.27: The sitemap shows which pages matter, while robots.txt draws the boundaries of crawling. One wrong rule can leave critical pages out of the crawl, or drop the whole site out of the index; that's why regular checks are essential.
ceviri.28: What does setting up structured data (schema) achieve?
ceviri.29: Schema markup describes the type of information on a page to the search engine in plain terms. That way rich results — a rating, frequently asked questions, or service details — can appear in the listings and the result stands out.
ceviri.30: How does a professional technical SEO audit differ from free online tools?
ceviri.31: Free tools give you a general idea, but they often can't see the deeper problems tied to server configuration or the JavaScript render process. A professional audit uses their output only as a first layer, and confirms the real findings at server and code level.

ceviri.65: How does Core Web Vitals measure page performance?
ceviri.66: One of Google's ranking signals, Core Web Vitals measures how fast a page loads, how quickly it responds to interaction, and how visually stable it is.
ceviri.67: LCP assesses how quickly the largest content block reaches the screen, INP the response given to an interaction, and CLS the sudden shifts during loading. When these metrics come out weak, the search engine judges the user experience inadequate and leaves the page behind. In the audit, render-blocking resources are stripped out, images are converted to modern formats and compressed, critical CSS is brought forward, unnecessary third-party scripts are pared back and the server response time is improved. Because of mobile-first indexing, all of these measurements are tested on the mobile experience first. Performance work isn't a one-off; every update can move the metrics again, so it calls for regular monitoring.
ceviri.69: Crawlability, Search Console and Structured Data
ceviri.70: Before a search engine can rank a page, it first has to find and crawl it, and then index it.
ceviri.71: Sitemap.xml acts as a map showing the site's priority pages; robots.txt describes which sections are not to be crawled. When one of these files is set up wrongly the consequences can be severe: a wrong robots.txt rule can close the whole site to crawling, and a broken sitemap delays new pages entering the index. Redirect chains, broken links and inconsistent canonical tags are also problems that waste crawl budget, and they are put right one by one in the audit. Search Console integration is the verification layer for this work; the coverage report shows which pages are indexed and the reason any others are left out. Structured data — that is, schema markup — explains the meaning of the page content to the search engine in machine language; correctly marked-up service or question-and-answer data can produce rich results in the listings. ceviri.134: The Scope of the Technical Audit
ceviri.135: The audit works through a checklist covering crawl and index status, server responses, security configuration, internal linking architecture and mobile compatibility. Each finding is classified by how far it affects the site's communication with the search engine.
ceviri.137: Errors that block indexing go to the top of the list, followed by problems that weaken performance and user experience. Fine tuning such as schema enrichment comes into play once the foundations are solid.
ceviri.139: The recommended fixes are put into effect in a way that suits the site's existing structure. After implementation, the coverage and performance data in Search Console are monitored so the real effect is confirmed.
